payload.text:
[owner spec 2026-08-22, measured] Ten 'not measured' cells on the live page, six per lane card. The owner's words: the cards have properties that are always 'not measured' so it only crowds the cards and gives no valuable info.

WHAT A LIVE CARD ACTUALLY SHOWS on the served page right now, per card:
  agent      claude · cla…        <- present, and the model is TRUNCATED to 'cla…'
  running    not measured
  tokens     not measured  (or a real figure once the stream reports)
  cost usd   not measured
  context    not measured
  rework     not measured

So four to five of six rows are placeholders, and the one present row is clipped so hard the model is unreadable - which matters more now that a run can dispatch at a different tier and the model is the thing an operator wants to compare.

TWO SEPARATE FIXES, and they are not the same:
1. A row with no value draws no row. This record.
2. The agent/model cell needs room the placeholders are currently spending. That falls out of 1 for free and should be verified rather than assumed - after removing four rows, check the model renders in full.

WHY THE COUNT WILL NOT REACH ZERO, and why that is correct: running, cost and context are per-dispatch figures that do not exist yet for a live lane, and basicly-0hxck3 deliberately refuses to carry the previous dispatch's forward - that would print last run's spend under a heading saying the lane runs now. So the absence is right and printing it is wrong. Do not 'fix' this by filling them.

Live elapsed is a real gap rather than a correct absence: no start time exists on LaneStream, on LaneView or anywhere on disk, because the run record is written after the process ends. It is a separate follow-on and not this record.

payload.acceptance_criteria:
- When no comment policy is configured, installation and upgrade shall retain strict whole-file prose refusal.
- When no-comment-ratchet is selected, the shared standalone comments kit shall refuse new, changed, duplicate, multiline and deletion-created prose while allowing unchanged legacy prose and legitimate renames.
- When a scan, baseline read or subprocess fails, both policies shall refuse the operation without modifying consumer files.
- When hooks execute on Windows, Linux or macOS, Unicode output, repository-relative check and fix programs, shared snapshots and original Git arguments shall preserve their meaning and failure status.
- When a consumer has an unsupported project interpreter, managed launchers shall request Python 3.14 or later without excluding later supported minor versions.
- When native Git hooks run for an initial or ordinary commit, foreign hooks and staged checks shall execute with preserved arguments, partial staging and deliberate refusal.
- When the integrated candidate is ready, focused native platform checks, projection checks and full repository verification shall pass, with consumer evidence recorded for release preparation.

payload.name: acceptance_criteria
payload.value:
- When no comment policy is configured, installation and upgrade shall retain strict whole-file prose refusal.
- When no-comment-ratchet is selected, the shared standalone comments kit shall refuse new, changed, duplicate, multiline and deletion-created prose while allowing unchanged legacy prose and legitimate renames.
- When a scan, baseline read or subprocess fails, both policies shall refuse the operation without modifying consumer files.
- When hooks execute on Windows, Linux or macOS, Unicode output, repository-relative check and fix programs, shared snapshots and original Git arguments shall preserve their meaning and failure status.
- When a consumer has an unsupported project interpreter, managed launchers shall request Python 3.14 or later without excluding later supported minor versions.
- When native Git hooks run for an initial or ordinary commit, foreign hooks and staged checks shall execute with preserved arguments, partial staging and deliberate refusal.
- When the integrated candidate is ready, focused native platform checks, projection checks and full repository verification shall pass, with consumer evidence recorded for release preparation.
- When a consumer uses a permanent install URL, the installer shall select the latest released wheel with Python 3.14 or later and propagate installation failure without prompting.

payload.name: acceptance_criteria
payload.value:
- When no comment policy is configured, installation and upgrade shall retain strict whole-file prose refusal.
- When no-comment-ratchet is selected, the shared standalone comments kit shall refuse new, changed, duplicate, multiline and deletion-created prose while allowing unchanged legacy prose and legitimate renames.
- When a scan, baseline read or subprocess fails, both policies shall refuse the operation without modifying consumer files.
- When hooks execute on Windows, Linux or macOS, Unicode output, repository-relative check and fix programs, shared snapshots and original Git arguments shall preserve their meaning and failure status.
- When a consumer has an unsupported project interpreter, managed launchers shall request Python 3.14 or later without excluding later supported minor versions.
- When native Git hooks run for an initial or ordinary commit, foreign hooks and staged checks shall execute with preserved arguments, partial staging and deliberate refusal.
- When the integrated candidate is ready, focused native platform checks, projection checks and full repository verification shall pass, with consumer evidence recorded for release preparation.
- When a consumer uses a permanent install URL, the installer shall select the latest released wheel with Python 3.14 or later and propagate installation failure without prompting.
- When the maintainer rebuilds the Windows-only Lefthook patch, both archives shall match pinned bytes and checksums while Linux and macOS retain official archives.

payload.description:
## Context

A site `basicly-vrgi1jk` missed, found by running the command rather than the tests, one hour after that record closed.

The decision (basicly-hnnmk9.1) was that the token budget measures and never blocks. Seven `spend.halted` consumers were converted. `loop preflight` builds its own verdict in `cli.py` and was not among them:

```
$ basicly loop preflight basicly-k6tpep --label board-throughput
grant:     L3, spent 104485469 under it, remaining 0
VERDICT:   not ready - the grant is spent
```

## The two sites

`cli.py:3596-3607` appends two blockers that are spend facts:

```python
if status.halted:
    print(f"halted:    {status.detail}")
    blockers.append(... "the grant budget is spent")
if (metered := supervise.metered_without_a_budget(repo_root, status)) is not None:
    print(f"budget:    MISSING - ...")
    blockers.append("a metered runner needs a grant with a token budget")
```

Both already **print** their line. Only the `blockers.append` has to go, so the figure survives and the verdict stops.

## Why the tests did not catch it

`basicly-vrgi1jk` inverted nineteen tests that asserted a refusal in the engine. `preflight` composes its verdict in the CLI from a list of strings, and no test asserted that spend was absent from that list. The record own acceptance criterion said *"WHEN spend passes a budget, NO code path SHALL refuse"*, and the sweep was over `spend.halted` call sites in `src/basicly/*.py` minus `cli.py`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN a grant is past its budget, `loop preflight` SHALL still print `halted:` and the figure, and SHALL NOT add a blocker for it.
- WHEN a metered runner has no budget, `loop preflight` SHALL still print `budget: MISSING` and SHALL NOT add a blocker for it.
- A TEST SHALL assert the verdict of a preflight whose only fault is spend, so the blocker cannot come back.
- WHERE a blocker is not a spend fact, the verdict SHALL be unchanged.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/cli.py`
- `tests/test_cli_loop.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L2`
- demonstration: run `loop preflight` on a root whose grant is spent and read `VERDICT: ready`

## Context

`[[verify.checks]]` spells lint-imports as a bare command (`command = ["lint-imports"]`), so it
resolves from PATH. A landing runs verify as a subprocess of `basicly loop advance`, which was
launched with `uv run` from the base checkout, so PATH carries the base `.venv/bin` and
import-linter imports the `basicly` package the *base* editable install points at.

lint-imports is the only configured check that resolves its target by import rather than by path -
pyright and vulture read files under cwd - so it is the only one that follows the venv instead of
the worktree.

## Steps to Reproduce

Measured 2026-08-08 on the basicly-u2hl.2 worktree, which adds `src/basicly/integrity.py`:

```text
VIRTUAL_ENV=<base>/.venv PATH=<base><redacted:posix-absolute-path>:$PATH lint-imports
  -> Missing layer in container 'basicly': module basicly.integrity does not exist.
uv run lint-imports
  -> Contracts: 2 kept, 0 broken.
```

## Impact

Any lane that adds a new module can never land: the gate reports a module-not-found the lane's tree
does not have, and the bounded rework loop cannot fix it. basicly-u2hl.2 escalated at rework 2/2
with the engine's own note that 'this round changed nothing it reports'. Two lanes' landings and
one rework round were spent on it.

## Scope

- `basicly.toml`
- `tests/test_verify.py`

payload.description:
## Context

`basicly-imnu.9` added section 2.11 to `docs/research/2026-07-26-sota-review.md` on 2026-07-30 and
put a factually wrong claim in it. The claim was written from gastown's README, fetched rather than
read from source:

> **Take - their merge queue is ahead of ours in one specific, adoptable way.** [...] Gastown
> *bisects* on verification failure [...] Bisecting is a pure throughput win with no new dependency
> and no LLM in the loop [...] worth filing against `merge.py`.

**The batch-then-bisect merge queue is dead code.** Verified in the clone at `649b832`:
`AssembleBatch` and `ProcessBatch` appear only at their own definitions
(`internal/refinery/batch.go:58`, `:211`) with no call sites outside tests; the config field that
would enable them is never read (`engineer.go:177-179`); `ProcessMRInfo` (`engineer.go:1321`) has no
callers at all including tests; and the Go merge engine is unreachable because the Refinery is a
Claude agent in a tmux session, with the Go-driven foreground mode returning a hard error -
*"foreground mode is deprecated; use background mode"* (`internal/refinery/manager.go:154-156`). The
agent runbook says it processes the queue **sequentially**
(`.claude/commands/patrol.md:126`). `README.md:96` and `:653-661` describe an algorithm the shipped
binary cannot run.

So the corrected conclusion inverts the original one: **basicly's strictly serial queue is ahead of
what gastown actually runs, and deterministic where gastown's is an LLM.** The full analysis also
computed bisection's break-even at a per-lane pass rate of about 0.86 for a batch of five, for
roughly 2,100 lines and a blame defect that would corrupt the coupling graph - so it should not be
filed as work, which is the opposite of what section 2.11 currently recommends.

The durable lesson is the one this repo already has a rule for and I broke anyway: a README claim is
not evidence. The first pass read gastown through a fetched README summary; every corrected fact
here came from reading source. Record that in the section rather than quietly fixing the text.

## Scope

Also absorb the other six repos from the 2026-07-30 analysis, which currently live only in
`reference-repos/_analysis/` outside the repo: `oh-my-agent`, `oh-my-openagent`, `symphony`, `ccpm`,
`Archon`, `hankweave-runtime`. One subsection each, adopt and reject, with the `file:line` evidence
that supports it - so the review is the synthesis input for the new implementation plan rather than
a set of files on one machine.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given section 2.11 when it is read after this change then it records that the batch-then-bisect queue is unreachable code with the evidence, states that basicly's serial queue is ahead of what gastown runs, withdraws the recommendation to build bisecting, and names the readme-is-not-evidence failure that produced the original claim, and the other six analysed repos each have a subsection with adopt and reject findings
payload.title: Correct the gastown merge-queue claim and absorb the seven-repo analysis

payload.description:
## Context

Owner decision 2026-07-30, after the seven-repo sweep put the question on the table: **the loop's
phases stay engine code. Declarative phases are rejected, not deferred.**

Two of the analysed projects had made phases declarative - Archon a Zod-validated node DAG in
`.archon/workflows/*.yaml`, Symphony an engine that knows only three predicates with the lifecycle in
`WORKFLOW.md` front matter - so the option was real and worth answering rather than ignoring.

Three reasons, in the order that decided it:

1. **The part that would have to move cannot move safely.** `derive_phase`
   (`src/basicly/loop_state.py:106-143`) is a five-rung predicate ladder, and most rungs are
   mechanical enough to express as data. The exception is the `verified` term -
   `gates.can_advance and (worktree is not None or has_children)`, plus ship's
   `(worktree is None or verified)`. That encodes the *landed* invariant found by incident
   `basicly-k35r`: approving ship before the landing wedged the phase with no route back to the
   merge. Expressed in YAML it becomes a boolean expression language, and the invariant lives where
   pyright cannot check it, the test suite cannot easily target it, and review will not catch a
   subtle edit. The general form of the cost is worth stating once: **every rule that moves from
   code to data leaves the type checker, the test suite, and code review.**
2. **Nobody has asked.** Zero beads request configurable phases, no consumer has raised it, and the
   eight phases were stable through the entire factory build. The repo rule is to solve the stated
   requirement rather than build a speculative abstraction.
3. **What a consumer would actually want to vary is already configuration** - `required_gates`,
   `max_rework`, the verify checks per mode, and the autonomy levels all live in `basicly.toml`.
   The demand that declarative phases would serve is largely already served.

Record honestly what the evidence does *not* show. It is tempting to argue that declarativeness
caused the determinism failures in those two projects; it did not. Archon's flaw is a disjunction in
a completion gate (`dag-executor.ts:4602`) and Symphony's is having no persistence at all. Both are
independent design errors in projects that also happened to be configurable. The correlation is not
causation, and the reason to reject is the typed-invariant argument above, not guilt by association.

Two things are adopted independently of this rejection and must not be lost with it:

- `basicly-m4zv.13` - Archon's evidence-artifact presence check, which needs no phase machinery.
- Symphony's three-predicate engine is worth reading as a **simplification prompt** for our own
  ladder rather than as a config feature: if an engine can drive a seven-stage lifecycle knowing
  only active/terminal/neither, our five rungs deserve a look for accidental complexity. Filed
  separately.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the architecture reference and the implementation plan when each is read after this change then both record that phases stay engine code with the landed-invariant reason and the no-recorded-demand reason, both note that the correlation with those projects' determinism failures is not causation, and the plan states that declarative phases are not on the roadmap
payload.title: Record that phases stay engine code and declarative phases are rejected

payload.description:
## Context

The licence review of the seven repos swept on 2026-07-30 found **two rider-class restrictions that
the LICENSE file alone does not reveal** - the same class of finding as the `beads_rust` rider that
`references.md` section 2 exists to record. Analysis in
`reference-repos/_analysis/licenses.md`.

Five are clean stock licences: `gastown` MIT (Steve Yegge, 2025, diffed byte-exact), `oh-my-agent`
MIT, `openai/symphony` genuine stock Apache-2.0 with `NOTICE`, `ccpm` MIT (grant covers the markdown,
which matters because the reuse there is methodology and prose), `Archon` MIT. No licence file was
missing anywhere.

**`oh-my-openagent` is not open source.** `LICENSE.md` is the **Sustainable Use License 1.0**
(non-OSI): *"You may use or modify the software only for your own internal business purposes or for
non-commercial or personal use. You may distribute the software or provide it to others only if you do
so free of charge for non-commercial purposes."* Confirmed that the three files cited in review
section 2.12 - `model-resolution-pipeline.ts`, `category-model-requirements.ts`,
`model-settings-compatibility.ts` - all live under `packages/model-core/src/`, and **`model-core` has
no LICENSE of its own**, so the root SUL governs them. Only `pi-goal`, `pi-webfetch` and
`lsp-tools-mcp` carry their own; `omo-senpi/plugin/LICENSE` is a scoped MIT covering six named
portions only.

**`hankweave-runtime` carries a competition restriction through its `NOTICE.md`**, not its LICENSE:
*"By using Hankweave, you agree to Southbridge AI's Terms of Service"*, whose key provisions include
*"Competition restrictions on using Hanks to build competing products"* and *"Managed services
restrictions require prior written consent"*. basicly is a coding-agent harness and hankweave an
agent-orchestration runtime, so the restriction plausibly reaches us. Whether a NOTICE can bind at all
is genuinely unsettled - Apache-2.0 says notices are informational - and that is a question for
someone qualified, not for this bead to resolve.

## What is actually wrong in the repo right now

Two things were committed that these terms do not support, and both are mine:

1. **Review section 2.12** recommends the oh-my-openagent tier logic as *"about 400 lines of pure
   logic that ports to stdlib Python unchanged"*. Under the SUL that is not an available option.
2. **`basicly-vkh0.9`** and the **`basicly-kjc5.58` comment** carry the same recommendation shape -
   adopt these mechanisms, with source line ranges as the reference.

The sharp part: section 2.12 already contains the warning that *"reusing any of this text or deriving
an implementation from a quoted snippet requires reading that project's LICENSE first"* - written in
the same commit that then recommended derivation from two repos whose licences had not been read. The
warning was right and was not followed.

**What survives, and it is most of the value.** A licence restricts copying expression, not learning a
fact. The *measurements* stay usable and are the strongest findings: hankweave's own committed fixture
having 44.5% of events share a millisecond is a measured property of published data, not their code.
The *concepts* - declare a tier rather than a model id, return a provenance enum, clamp an unsupported
setting and record the downgrade, carry a running aggregate so the tail answers the common query - are
ideas. What must stop is treating their source as the implementation reference: no port, no snippet,
no line-by-line transcription, exactly the clean-room posture section 2.10 already sets for
`beads_rust`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given references.md when it is read after this change then all seven repos appear in the section 1 table with revision and reuse verdict, the two restricted licences have their operative clause quoted and their consequence stated, and review section 2.12 and beads vkh0.9 and kjc5.58 no longer recommend porting or deriving from either restricted source while keeping the measurements and concepts that are unaffected
payload.title: Record the two restricted licences and withdraw the derivation recommendations

payload.acceptance_criteria: When an arm runs then the harness reads back the guidance live in that cell and fails if it does not match the arm's declaration
payload.description:
## Context

Plan section 10's second owed owner decision, **taken 2026-08-14: design the arms now.** It had been
owed since the plan was rewritten on 2026-08-08 and had no owner; architecture section 14.4 names the
shape and nothing is built.

The owner chose this over deferring it past v1.0.0.

## What is owed

Two things, and the second is the sharper one.

**The four arms.** Architecture section 14.4 names the shape of a catalog eval but not the arms
themselves. An arm is a cell whose guidance configuration is declared, so a measured difference
between arms is attributable to that configuration and to nothing else.

**Whether the safety tier is a gate or a metric.** A metric reports; a gate refuses. This repository
has a recorded rule for exactly that call - D23: a control with no recorded correct firing becomes
observability, and one that has earned a firing keeps its teeth. A safety tier that has never fired
starts as a metric under that rule, and the decision is whether safety is the exception.

## The constraints this design must honour, each already recorded

- **The isolation assertion is the whole instrument.** Plan section 11 names the risk: *"a measurement
  is uninterpretable because an arm was contaminated"*, and the remedy already written is that the
  harness reads back what guidance is live in the cell and fails if it does not match the arm's
  declaration. Without that, every number the eval produces is unfalsifiable.
- **Stage by adding entries to the enforced set, never by lowering a threshold.** Also plan section 11.
  Tier-1 failure from the start.
- **8 of 34 skills had ever been exercised** when last measured, and that figure is now unsound
  (`basicly-4grf`) because `ey58` injects a role's skills into the dispatch prompt, so the never-used
  report cannot tell an uninvoked skill from an injected one. **The eval needs a sound exercised-count
  before it can measure anything about guidance**, so state whether this bead depends on `4grf` or
  routes around it.
- **An unmeasured behavioural claim costs context every turn** - the plan's third invariant. That is
  the argument for the eval and it is also the standard the eval itself is held to.

## Acceptance

- When the four arms are declared, then each names its guidance configuration and what a difference
  between it and its neighbour would establish.
- When an arm runs, then the harness reads back the guidance live in that cell and fails if it does not
  match the declaration.
- When the safety tier is decided, then the decision states whether it gates or reports and cites the
  rule that decided it.
- When the design lands, then it states what it depends on for a sound exercised-count and does not
  assume the 8-of-34 figure.

## Scope

Design only. `docs/architecture/architecture.md` section 14.4 is the target of the write-up; the
implementation is decomposed after.

## Demonstration

The four arms are readable by someone who was not in the room, and for each one a reader can say what
result would falsify it. A design nobody can falsify is the thing this eval exists to catch.

payload.acceptance_criteria: Given a written ceremony threshold when a change touches src or catalog sources then the harness loop is required and when a change is docs-only or tracker-only or config-only then a named lightweight path applies that skips the ceremony but never the hooks and the rule is stated as an imperative constraint rather than descriptive prose
payload.description:
## Context

Plan §7.1, resolved by owner decision 2026-07-26. The decision is made; this bead implements it.

DECIDED: the threshold is the touched path. The harness loop is required for any change touching `src/**` or catalog sources under `.basicly/**`. A docs-only, tracker-only, or config-only change may take a lightweight path.

Chosen because it is the only form of the rule that can be enforced rather than hoped for: a hook can check which paths a commit touches. The rule today mandates the loop for "non-trivial work", which is the agents own judgment call, so the rule is currently unenforceable - every loop decision this repo has made was an agent choosing to comply. A diff-size threshold was rejected as a poor proxy: a one-line change to a gate or a hook is exactly the kind of edit that most needs the ceremony.

The lightweight path skips the ceremony and never the hooks. That is the whole point of naming it - an unnamed escape hatch becomes "skip the loop" and then "skip the gates".

## Notes

The threshold belongs in the always-on Harness Loop fragment, and the recall measurement under basicly-agzx.1 is a reason to keep it short: content phrased as an imperative constraint is retrieved, descriptive prose is not - the one rule that scored 0/3 in both families was the only non-imperative line in the file.

Consider whether a hook can assert it, since that is the justification for choosing this form over the alternatives. If it cannot be asserted, say so rather than shipping an unenforceable rule in different words.

## Scope

payload.name: description
payload.value:
## Trigger

When a change touches `src/**` or a catalog source under `.basicly/**`, I want the harness loop required and a named lightweight path for everything else, so I can enforce the ceremony by the touched path instead of by an agent's own judgement.

## Context

Plan §7.1, resolved by owner decision 2026-07-26. The decision is made; this bead implements it.

DECIDED: the threshold is the touched path. The harness loop is required for any change touching `src/**` or catalog sources under `.basicly/**`. A docs-only, tracker-only, or config-only change may take a lightweight path.

Chosen because it is the only form of the rule that can be enforced rather than hoped for: a hook can check which paths a commit touches. The rule today mandates the loop for "non-trivial work", which is the agents own judgment call, so the rule is currently unenforceable - every loop decision this repo has made was an agent choosing to comply. A diff-size threshold was rejected as a poor proxy: a one-line change to a gate or a hook is exactly the kind of edit that most needs the ceremony.

The lightweight path skips the ceremony and never the hooks. That is the whole point of naming it - an unnamed escape hatch becomes "skip the loop" and then "skip the gates".

## Notes

The threshold belongs in the always-on Harness Loop fragment, and the recall measurement under basicly-agzx.1 is a reason to keep it short: content phrased as an imperative constraint is retrieved, descriptive prose is not - the one rule that scored 0/3 in both families was the only non-imperative line in the file.

Consider whether a hook can assert it, since that is the justification for choosing this form over the alternatives. If it cannot be asserted, say so rather than shipping an unenforceable rule in different words.

## Scope

- `.basicly/core/fragments/project/harness-loop.fragment.yaml`
- `docs/design/steering-surfaces-design.md`

## Context

`docs/research/2026-07-26-sota-review.md` section 5 lists six "real, structural leads". Two of
them are now overstated, verified against sources on 2026-07-30:

- Lead 1, "enforcement is code and git hooks, not prose", and lead 3, "agent-agnostic
  projection from one catalog - others ship per-host adapters maintained by hand ... we
  generate, and we gate the generation". `first-fluke/oh-my-agent` keeps `.agents/` as a single
  source of truth, projects it into each runtime's native layout via `oma emit`
  (Agent-Skills-conformant skill folders, `AGENTS.md`, `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`), and
  ships "a drift check in CI keeping the generated output honest" plus `oma verify <agent>`, a
  deterministic per-agent check battery.

So generate-and-gate is no longer differentiating on its own. What survives is narrower and
should be stated precisely: oh-my-agent installs **no git hooks** - its drift check is CI-only -
so our edge is enforcement at *commit time*, which is a different guarantee from a check that
fails the build afterwards. It also has no autonomous ticket-driven loop, no worktrees and no
merge queue.

The review was also written before six comparables the owner surfaced. The most important is
`gastownhall/gastown`, from the same org as the beads tracker section 2.10 already analyses. It
covers the orchestration half in full - worktree-isolated agents, a Bors-style merge queue that
bisects to isolate a failing MR, a supervisor patrol tier, human-gated convoys - in Go, and it
requires `bd` 0.57+ **plus Dolt plus tmux 3.0+**.

That does not make our orchestration redundant, and the review should say why: Gastown sits on
the DB-authoritative fork section 2.10 deliberately diverged from, so it is evidence the fork is
real and widening rather than evidence we are reinventing. Our dependency floor on that half is
materially lighter - no database, no daemon, no terminal multiplexer.

Also not yet covered: `oh-my-openagent`, `Archon` (YAML phases plus worktrees plus validation
gates), `openai/symphony` (ticket-driven isolated runs), `hankweave` (checkpoint-gated
resumability over existing harnesses), `CCPM` (PRD to parallel agents over GitHub Issues).

- Given the SOTA review when section 5 is read after this change then leads 1 and 3 state the narrowed commit-time claim with oh-my-agent named as the project that matches the CI-gated projection, and the review records Gastown as covering the orchestration half on the DB-authoritative fork with our lighter dependency floor as the stated difference

payload.description:
## Steps to Reproduce

```
rg -n "zero lanes have failed" src/basicly/config.py
uv run python -c "
from pathlib import Path
from basicly import run_record
h = run_record.dispatch_history(Path('.'))
print({o: sum(1 for b,hh in h.items() for e in hh if e.get('outcome')==o)
       for o in {e.get('outcome') for b,hh in h.items() for e in hh}})
print([(b, e.get('returncode'), e.get('scope_tokens'))
       for b,hh in h.items() for e in hh if e.get('outcome')=='failed'])
"
```

Observed - the comment asserts no lane has ever failed, and the history reports `{'failed': 4, 'handoff': 181, 'executed': 23}`. Expected - the recorded rationale matches the record.

## Context

`basicly-3w44` raised the ceiling to 112000 and the value is right, but the reasoning committed beside it is wrong in a way worth fixing loudly, because the error is instructive.

**The false claim.** `config.py` says "Zero lanes have failed at any size, so this is a LOWER bound on a safe ceiling". There are **four failed dispatches**, all `returncode 143` (SIGTERM), across `basicly-kjc5.42`, `kjc5.43` and `kjc5.44`.

**Why they were missed - survivorship bias in the analysis itself.** The query that produced "47 lanes, zero failed" filtered on `isinstance(entry.get('scope_tokens'), int)`. **Every failed lane records `scope_tokens=None`**, so the filter excluded the entire failure population by construction and the conclusion was an artifact of the measurement. This is the same defect class the bead was filed to fix - a number that does not measure what it is read as measuring - committed by the fix for it.

**The value survives on better evidence.** Sizing the failed beads from the tree:

| Lane | Estimate | vs 112000 |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| `tcmy.31` largest completed | 105318 | admitted |
| ceiling | 112000 | |
| `kjc5.42` failed | 136668 | refused |
| `kjc5.44` failed | 136668 | refused |
| `kjc5.43` failed | 5734 | admitted - a 3823-token scope, so a timeout, not a size failure |

So 112000 separates the observed successes from the two large observed failures. That is a genuinely separating boundary and a far stronger justification than "nothing has failed yet".

**The gate is half a gate.** `test_the_ceiling_does_not_refuse_a_size_that_has_already_succeeded` binds one direction only. Now that failures are known to exist and are sizeable, the ceiling must also not **admit** a size that failed for size reasons. A one-directional gate would have let this error through, and did.

Note the `scope_tokens=None` on failures is itself a finding for `basicly-3w44` (b): a lane that dies records nothing about what it was sizing, so the most informative samples are the ones the telemetry drops.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the ceiling rationale in config.py when it is read then it states the separating boundary between observed successes and observed failures and makes no claim that zero lanes have failed
- Given a completed lane and a failed lane when the ceiling gate runs then it fails if the ceiling would refuse a success and also fails if it would admit a size that failed for size reasons
- Given a lane that fails when its dispatch is recorded then the record carries the scope cost it was sized on so failures are not silently excluded from any later analysis

## Scope

- `src/basicly/config.py`
